arxiv-2205-04912.title: Quantum phase transitions in a bidimensional 𝑶 ⁡ ( 𝑵 ) × ℤ 𝟐 O(N)\times{\mathbb{Z}_{2}} scalar field model arXiv: 2205.04912 [hep-th]
arxiv-2205-04912.creator: Gustavo O. Heymans, Marcus Benghi Pinto, and Rudnei O. Ramos
arxiv-2205-04912.description: Abstract We analyze the possible quantum phase transition patterns occurring within the O ⁡ ( N ) × ℤ 2 O(N)\times{\mathbb{Z}_{2}} scalar multi-field model at vanishing temperatures in ( 1 + 1 ) (1+1) -dimensions. The physical masses associated with the two coupled scalar sectors are evaluated using the loop approximation up to second order.

arxiv-2212-07438.title: The perspective of voids on rising cosmology tensions
arxiv-2212-07438.creator: S. Contarini 1,2,3, A. Pisani 4,5,6, N. Hamaus 7, F. Marulli 1,2,3, L. Moscardini 1,2,3, M. Baldi 1,2,3
arxiv-2212-07438.description: Abstract We investigate the main tensions within the current standard model of cosmology from the perspective of the main statistics of cosmic voids, using the final BOSS DR12 data set. For this purpose, we present the first estimate of the S 8 ≡ σ 8 ​ Ω m / 0.3 S_{8}\equiv\sigma_{8}\sqrt{\Omega_{\rm m}/0.

arxiv-2307-10910.title: Maximal colourings for graphs
arxiv-2307-10910.creator: Raffaella Mulas
arxiv-2307-10910.description: Abstract We consider two different notions of graph colouring, namely, the t t -periodic colouring for vertices that has been introduced in 1974 by Bondy and Simonovits, and the periodic colouring for oriented edges that has been recently introduced in the context of spectral theory of non-backtracking operators.

arxiv-2311-17059.title: Mission-driven Exploration for Accelerated Deep Reinforcement Learning with Temporal Logic Task Specifications
arxiv-2311-17059.creator: Jun Wang, Hosein Hasanbeig, Kaiyuan Tan, Zihe Sun, Yiannis Kantaros
arxiv-2311-17059.description: Abstract \textcolor black This paper addresses the problem of designing control policies for agents with unknown stochastic dynamics and control objectives specified using Linear Temporal Logic (LTL). Recent Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL) algorithms have aimed to compute policies that maximize the satisfaction probability of LTL formulas, but they often suffer from slow learning performance.

arxiv-2312-00809.title: Off-shell modifications of bound nucleons and parton distributions
arxiv-2312-00809.creator: S. I. Alekhin, S. A. Kulagin, R. Petti
arxiv-2312-00809.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by S. I. Alekhin, S. A. Kulagin, R. Petti. We discuss results from our global QCD analyses including nuclear data off deuterium from various measurements, as well as off H 3 {}^{3}\text{H} and He 3 {}^{3}\text{He} targets from the MARATHON experiment. We simultaneously determine the parton distribution functions of the proton, the higher-twist terms, and the nucleon off-shell correction functions responsible for the modifications of the partonic structure in bound protons and neutrons.

arxiv-2403-09425.title: Fixing two points in primitive solvable groups
arxiv-2403-09425.creator: Francesca Lisi and Luca Sabatini
arxiv-2403-09425.description: Abstract . Consider a finite primitive solvable group. We observe that a result of Y. Yang implies that there exist two points whose pointwise stabilizer has derived length at most 9 9 . We show that, if the group has odd cardinality, then there exist two points whose pointwise stabilizer is abelian. 2020 Mathematics Subject Classification Primary: 20B15 1.

arxiv-2407-15154.title: Fine-grained Gender Control in Machine Translation with Large Language Models
arxiv-2407-15154.creator: Minwoo Lee Hyukhun Koh Minsung Kim Kyomin Jung
arxiv-2407-15154.description: Abstract In machine translation, the problem of ambiguously gendered input has been pointed out, where the gender of an entity is not available in the source sentence. To address this ambiguity issue, the task of controlled translation that takes the gender of the ambiguous entity as additional input have been proposed.

arxiv-2503-00557.title: Heatwave increases nighttime light intensity in hyperdense cities of the Global South: A double machine learning study
arxiv-2503-00557.creator: Ramit Debnath, Taran Chandel, Fengyuan Han, Ronita Bardhan
arxiv-2503-00557.description: Abstract Heatwaves, intensified by climate change and rapid urbanisation, pose significant threats to urban systems, particularly in the Global South, where adaptive capacity is constrained. This study investigates the relationship between heatwaves and nighttime light (NTL) radiance, a proxy of nighttime economic activity, in four hyperdense cities: Delhi, Guangzhou, Cairo, and São Paulo. We hypothesised that heatwaves increase nighttime activity.

arxiv-2503-01525.title: Global Blind Spot in Understanding Trigonometric Derivatives: A Multinational Analysis
arxiv-2503-01525.creator: Yossi Ben-Zion, Jianqiang Liu, Chun-Ming Wang, Atanu Rajak, Noah D. Finkelstein
arxiv-2503-01525.description: Abstract Trigonometric derivatives are fundamental in both mathematics and physics, yet their proper application, particularly the distinction between radians and degrees, poses a significant challenge for college students globally. This study identifies a widespread ”blind spot” in understanding trigonometric derivatives and their implications for physical systems, highlighting a critical gap in physics education.

arxiv-2505-02513.title: Trustworthy Inter-Provider Agreements in 6G Using a Privacy-Enabled Hybrid Blockchain Framework This work was partially supported by MCIN/AEI grant PID2021-126431OB-I00, “ERDF A way of making Europe”, Spanish MINECO grants TSI-063000-2021-54/-55 (6G-DAWN), and Generalitat de Catalunya grant 2021 SGR
arxiv-2505-02513.creator: Farhana Javed and Josep Mangues-Bafalluy
arxiv-2505-02513.description: Abstract Inter-provider agreements are central to 6G networks, where administrative domains must securely and dynamically share services. To address the dual need for transparency and confidentiality, we propose a privacy-enabled hybrid blockchain setup using Hyperledger Besu, integrating both public and private transaction workflows.

arxiv-2510-19304.title: Loopholing Discrete Diffusion: Deterministic Bypass of the Sampling Wall
arxiv-2510-19304.creator: Mingyu Jo, Jaesik Yoon, Justin Deschenaux, Caglar Gulcehre, Sungjin Ahn
arxiv-2510-19304.description: Abstract Discrete diffusion models offer a promising alternative to autoregressive generation through parallel decoding, but they suffer from a sampling wall: once categorical sampling occurs, rich distributional information collapses into one-hot vectors and cannot be propagated across steps, forcing subsequent steps to operate with limited information.

pmc-11475495.title: Enhancing Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer Survival Prediction through Multi-Omics Integration Using Graph Attention Network
pmc-11475495.creator: Murtada K Elbashir, Abdullah Almotilag, Mahmood A Mahmood, Mohanad Mohammed, Dechang Chen
pmc-11475495.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Background: Cancer survival prediction is vital in improving patients’ prospects and recommending therapies. Understanding the molecular behavior of cancer can be enhanced through the integration of multi-omics data, including mRNA, miRNA, and DNA methylation data. In light of these multi-omics data, we proposed a graph attention network (GAT) model in this study to predict the survival of non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC).

pmc-11508698.title: Endothelial Keratoplasty Following Glaucoma Filtration Surgery: A UK Tertiary Eye Care Referral Centre Experience
pmc-11508698.creator: Francesco Aiello, Francesco Matarazzo, Maria Phylactou, Kirithika Muthusamy, Vincenzo Maurino
pmc-11508698.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Purpose: To compare the postoperative complications and clinical outcomes of Descemet membrane endothelial keratoplasty (DMEK) and Descemet stripping automated endothelial keratoplasty (DSAEK) in eyes with previous glaucoma filtering surgery. Methods: In this retrospective comparative case series, we analysed postoperative visual acuity and intraocular pressure, graft survival, rate of graft detachment and/or dislocation, number of rebubbling and/or graft repositioning procedures, and graft rejection or failure (primary and secondary).

pmc-12391590.title: Functional and Phylogenetic Structure of Forest Bird Assemblages Along an Afrotropical Elevational Gradient
pmc-12391590.creator: Riccardo Pernice, Ondřej Sedláček, Tomáš Albrecht, Oldřich Tomášek, Ondřej Kauzál, Tereza Kauzálová, Francis Njie Motombi, Francis Luma Ewome, Michal Ferenc, Kryštof Chmel, Jiří Mlíkovský, Jan Riegert, Solange Mekuate Kamga, David Hořák
pmc-12391590.description: Elevational gradients offer valuable opportunities to investigate biodiversity patterns and the ecological and evolutionary processes that shape them. Although tropical mountains are recognized as biodiversity hotspots, the various dimensions of biodiversity in these systems, particularly in equatorial Africa, remain poorly understood.

pmc-12559853.title: Quantifying interest in and sentiment of online media about greenhouse gas emissions from cattle production in the United States
pmc-12559853.creator: Michael L Smith, Jinho Jung, Nicole Olynk Widmar, Danielle J Ufer, Maria Berikou, Jayson Lusk
pmc-12559853.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). The public is paying increased attention to the environmental impacts associated with cattle production systems in the US. Thus, cattle producers are increasingly exploring ways to communicate their efforts to reduce those environmental and climate impacts. This study uses online and social media data from 2018 to 2022 to examine public interest in and sentiment about beef and dairy cattle production when discussed within the context of greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions.

pmc-12646232.title: Inhibition of the inflammasome ameliorates orthologous polycystic kidney disease
pmc-12646232.creator: Junwei Liu, Manuel Rogg, Katharina Moos, Shaya Sasanpour, Vera Strassl, Manaswita Jain, Sato Magassa, Björn Neubauer, Simone Braeg, Benedikt S. Saller, Lisa Weißer, Frank Bienaimé, Oliver Gorka, Melanie Boerries, Amandine Viau, Olaf Gross, Christoph Schell, E. Wolfgang Kuehn
pmc-12646232.description: SignificanceAutosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease (ADPKD) is a common inherited kidney disorder and leads to kidney failure in most affected persons. No effective treatments exist. Characterized by cyst formation and kidney enlargement, inflammation has emerged as a crucial component, yet little information on specific pathways exists.

pmc-12715774.title: Neurological, metabolic and inflammatory phenotypes in a mouse model of ECHS1 deficiency
pmc-12715774.creator: Meghan M Eller, Aamir R Zuberi, Xiaorong Fu, Alina P Montalbano, Felix Nitschke, Shawn C Burgess, Cat Lutz, Rachel M Bailey
pmc-12715774.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). ECHS1 deficiency (ECHS1D) is a rare and devastating neurometabolic disease that currently has no defined treatments. This disorder results from missense loss-of-function mutations in the ECHS1 gene that results in severe developmental delays, encephalopathy, hypotonia and early death. ECHS1 enzymatic activity is necessary for the beta-oxidation of fatty acids and the oxidation of branched-chain amino acids within the inner mitochondrial matrix. The pathogenesis of disease remains poorly understood.

pmc-12866298.title: Sex-specific differences in the prognostic value of METS-IR for long-term outcomes in patients with MASLD and advanced liver fibrosis: a nationwide study
pmc-12866298.creator: Binbin Song, Yuan Zhou, Rui Su, Yan Wang, Song Chen, Wenjin Chen
pmc-12866298.description: ObjectiveInsulin resistance (IR) plays a critical role in shaping long-term outcomes in patients with metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD). Recent findings suggest that biological sex may influence the onset and progression of MASLD, yet it remains unclear whether sex modifies the link between IR and mortality in those with MASLD and advanced liver fibrosis.

pmc-13220790.creator: Ting Liu, Yiming Taclis Luo, Patrick Cheong-Iao Pang, Haopeng Zhang, Ao Xiang, Qin Yang, Bradley Malin
